1129.subject: Mathematics
1129.question_text: Find the principal which amounts to N5,500 at a simple interest in 5 years at 2% per annum.
1129.explanation:
Principal, P = Amount, A - Interest, I.
A = P + I

I = (P.T.R)/100 = (P x 5 x 2)/100 = 10P/100 = P/10

But A = P + I,
=> 5500 = P + (P/10)
=> 55000 = 10P + P
=> 55000 = 11P

Thus P = 55000/11 = N5,000

1149.subject: Mathematics
1149.question_text: If two graphs y = px\(^2\) + q and y = 2x\(^2\) -1 intersect at x = 2, find the value of p in terms q.
1149.explanation:
\(y = px^{2} + q ... (i)\)

\(y = 2x^{2} - 1 ... (ii)\)

At x = 2, 

(i): \(y = p(2^{2}) + q = 4p + q\)

(ii): \(y = 2(2^{2}) - 1 = 7\)

\(\therefore \text{The coordinates of the point of intersection = (2, 7)}\)

(i): \(7 = 4p + q \implies p = \frac{7 - q}{4}\)

1151.subject: Mathematics
1151.question_text:
Solve the equations
m2 + n2 = 29
m + n = 7
1151.explanation:
m2 + n2 = 29 .......(1)
m + n = 7 ............(2)

From (2),
m = 7 - n
but m2 + n2 = 29, substituting;
(7-n)2 + n2 = 29
49 - 14n + n2 + n2 = 29
=> 2n2 -14n + 20 = 0
Thus n2 -7n + 10 = 0

Factorizing;
(n-5)(n-2) = 0
n - 5 = 0, => n = 5
n - 2 = 0, => n = 2.

When n = 5,
m + n = 7, => m = 2,

When n = 2,
m + n = 7, => m = 5.

Thus (m,n) = (5,2) and (2,5)

1156.question_text: A point P moves such that it is equidistant from Points Q and R. Find QR when PR = 8cm and angle PRQ = 30°

P° = 180° - 60°

p° = 120°.

: PQ = r, PR = q, QR = p

1515.subject: Mathematics
1515.question_text: A straight line makes an angle of 30° with the positive x-axis and cuts the y-axis at y = 5. Find the equation of the straight line.
1515.explanation:
Cos 30 = \(\frac{5}{\text{x}}\)
x cos 30 = 5, => x = 5\(\sqrt{3}\)

Coordinates of P = - 5\(\sqrt{3}\), 0
Coordinates of Q = 0, 5
Gradient of PQ = (y\(_2\) - y\(_1\)) (X\(_2\) - X\(_1\)) = \(\frac{(5 - 0)}{(0 - 5\sqrt{3}}\))
= \(\frac{5}{5\sqrt{3}}\) = \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\)

Equation of PQ = y - y\(_1\) = m (x -x\(_1\))
y - 0 = \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) (x -( -5\(\sqrt{3}\)))

Thus: \(\sqrt{3}\)y = x + 5\(\sqrt{3}\)

1518.subject: Mathematics
1518.question_text: Find the value of P if the line joining (P, 4) and (6, -2) is perpendicular to the line joining (2, P) and (-1, 3).
1518.explanation:
The line joining (P, 4) and (6, -2).

Gradient: \(\frac{-2 - 4}{6 - P} = \frac{-6}{6 - P}\)

The line joining (2, P) and (-1, 3)

Gradient: \(\frac{3 - P}{-1 - 2} = \frac{3 - P}{-3}\)

For perpendicular lines, the product of their gradient = -1.

\((\frac{-6}{6 - P})(\frac{3 - P}{-3}) = -1\)

\(\frac{6 - 2P}{6 - P} = -1 \implies 6 - 2P = P - 6\)

\(6 + 6 = P + 2P \implies P = \frac{12}{3} = 4\)

69977.subject: Mathematics
69977.question_text: Find the integral values of x and y satisfying the inequality 3y + 5x \(\leq\) 15, given that y > 0, y < 3, and x > 0.
69977.explanation:
From the constraint y < 3 and y > 0, the possible values for y are 1 and 2

When y = 1, 3y + 5x \(\leq\) 15

3 + 5x  \(\leq\) 15 ⇒ 5x  \(\leq\) 12 ⇒ 2.4

since x must be an integer greater than 0 but less than or equal to 2.4, the possible values of x are 1 and 2

When y = 2,  3y + 5x \(\leq\) 15 ⇒ 6 + 5x \(\leq\) 15 ⇒ 6 \(\leq\) 15 - 6 = 11 ⇒ x = 2.2

Again, Since x must be an integer greater than 0 and less than or equal to 2.2, the only possible integer value of x is 1

So, the pairs (x, y) that satisfy all the conditions are ( 1, 1), (1, 2) and (2, 1).
